edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: The proposed pathway combines changes in oxidative damage, inflammatory tone, hormone signaling, bile-acid metabolism, and exposure to food-derived carcinogens or protective phytochemicals. For Colorectal cancer, those pathways matter over years, so consistent long-term intake patterns are more informative than short interventions.
edges.summary: In middle-aged and older adults, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that low-dose aspirin tracks with lower risk of colorectal cancer. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
